problem:
For the functions $f(x)$ and $g(x),$ you are given the following data:

$$
f(0)=2,\,{f}^{′}(0)=2,\,g(0)=1,\,{g}^{′}(0)=2
$$

Compute $\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{f(x)}{g(x)})$ at $x=0.$

feedback.problem:
The values of functions $f(x)$ and $g(x)$ and their derivatives at $x=5$ are given in the table below. 

| $x$ | $f(x)$ | $g(x)$ | ${f}^{′}(x)$ | ${g}^{′}(x)$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $5$ | $3$ | $-2$ | $-4$ | $6$ |

Compute $\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{f(x)}{g(x)})$ at $x=5.$

${\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{f(x)}{g(x)})|}_{x=5}=$
{{field-1}}
feedback.worked_solution:
Using the quotient rule, we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{f(x)}{g(x)})=\frac{{f}^{′}(x)g(x)-f(x){g}^{′}(x)}{(g(x))^{2}}.
$$

At the point where $x=5$, this gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{f(x)}{g(x)})|}_{x=5} & =\frac{{f}^{′}(5)g(5)-f(5){g}^{′}(5)}{(g(5))^{2}} \\  & =\frac{(-4)(-2)-(3)(6)}{(-2)^{2}} \\  & =\frac{8-18}{4} \\  & =-\frac{10}{4} \\  & =-\frac{5}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
